rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model provides a useful performance anchor. This tests the minimal RNA baseline using PCA and a single profile, isolating RNA representation without confounding effects from image data, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion. It is the best first use of budget because it is simple, likely cheap to train, and provides a reference point for later comparisons with image-only and multimodal settings.

Only a single RNA PCA single-profile baseline is available, so it is still unclear whether image features provide useful signal. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile model with a standard ResNet50, establishing a unimodal image baseline and isolating the modality decision while keeping the profile setting simple. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces major uncertainty about whether to invest in multimodal fusion and avoids adding aggregation or fusion complexity before the value of the image modality is known.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet, indicating RNA is the more promising modality. It is still unclear whether using multiple profiles with simple aggregation improves over the current RNA baseline. config_002 keeps the same PCA RNA encoder and tests the minimal multiprofile extension with avgpool, helping isolate the effect of profile setting/aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest existing signal with a low-risk comparison before adding more complex encoders or multimodal fusion.

The strongest completed result is config_002 (RNA-only, multiprofile, PCA, avgpool), which clearly outperforms RNA singleprofile and weak image-only baselines. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool for multiprofile RNA. config_003 tests exactly that by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the promising RNA multiprofile PCA setup fixed. This is the best next use of budget because it directly extends the current best direction, isolates an important design choice, and avoids prematurely adding more complex multimodal components.

The strongest evidence so far is that PCA-based RNA with multiprofile avgpool is the best current setting (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), clearly above singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether a stronger single-cell RNA representation can improve this best RNA-only baseline. config_008 tests scGPT under the same multiprofile avgpool setting, changing only the RNA encoder, so it isolates representation quality. This is a high-value next step because it exploits the strongest known direction, has plausible immediate performance, and avoids confounding RNA improvements with image or fusion choices before the RNA component is better understood.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile avgpool with PCA is the strongest result so far (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), while image-only single ResNet50 is weak (accuracy 0.208). The key uncertainty is whether the image modality can become useful under the same multiprofile avgpool setting that helped RNA, before adding fusion complexity. config_011 tests image-only ResNet50 with multiprofile avgpool, directly extending the weak image-only baseline and mirroring the successful RNA profile/aggregation choice without changing the encoder or introducing fusion. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces uncertainty about image utility and helps decide whether multimodal ResNet50 fusion experiments are worth testing next.

The strongest evidence so far is for RNA multiprofile with avgpool, where PCA reaches 0.591 accuracy and 0.573 F1, outperforming transformer aggregation and scGPT avgpool; image-only models are weak. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation such as scvi_n200 can improve on PCA in this best-known setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, cleanly isolating the representation effect. Under a limited budget, this is more informative than moving directly to multimodal fusion because it clarifies the best RNA backbone first and avoids confounding encoder, profile, aggregation, and fusion choices.

RNA multiprofile scvi_n200 avgpool is currently the strongest direction, but image evidence is sparse because only ResNet50 has been tested and it performed poorly. config_014 tests whether a stronger image representation (ImageNet ViT-L) makes the image modality competitive while keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed to the better ResNet baseline (multiprofile avgpool), cleanly isolating the image encoder effect. This is a high-value use of the next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about whether image features are worth pursuing before investing in multimodal fusion, even if it may not have the highest immediate accuracy.

The strongest evidence is RNA multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool, which achieved the best validation accuracy and F1. Image-only models are much weaker, so the next priority is to clarify whether the best RNA representation can be improved by changing aggregation. For PCA, avgpool outperformed transformer, but this has not been tested for scvi_n200. config_006 keeps the promising scvi_n200 multiprofile setting and changes only aggregation to transformer, making it a clean, high-value exploitation experiment before investing budget in more complex multimodal fusion.

RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile is currently the strongest direction, with validation accuracy around 0.650-0.653 and F1 around 0.628. Multiprofile also clearly helped pca_n200, but it is still unclear whether scvi_n200 would perform well without multiprofile aggregation. config_004 tests scvi_n200 with singleprofile, changing only the profile/aggregation setting relative to the best RNA-only models, so it isolates the effect of profile setting while staying close to the current best evidence. This is a controlled, high-information experiment before adding the larger uncertainty of multimodal fusion.
